newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Salvesen EGM approves special dividend.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Salvesen EGM approves special dividend.

text.p: Shareholders of food distribution and packaging group Christian Salvesen Plc on Thursday approved the company's proposal to pay a 34p per share special dividend worth around 100 million pounds ($159.7 million).
The move came despite private shareholders forcing a full vote after defeating the proposal at an extraordinary meeting (EGM) by an initial show of hands.

The board had been braced for a stormy meeting after former chairman and Salvesen family member Sir Gerald Elliot decided to lead a revolt against the dividend vote and to call for a vote of no-confidence in the management. Elliot and his backers wanted the group to deal with the demerger of the Aggreko division at the same meeting instead of at an EGM later this year. After a two-hour meeting on Thursday, the board's dividend resolution was defeated by a show of hands. But it won through with 55 percent of the total votes, including proxies for those large investors which were not present.
The company also spoke of plans to implement a consolidation of share capital and increase Salvesen's borrowing powers to 110 percent gearing.

Chairman Sir Alick Rankin said the move was the only way forward to ensure both company growth and enhance shareholder value. He said 16 UK and international banks had authorised borrowing at good rates of interest.

Elliot forecast more takeover bid approaches in the coming months similar to the offer made last summer by Hays Plc, the personnel and distribution group. "This will especially be the case if a second EGM planned by the Salvesen board votes for demerger of the company's successful Aggreko division," Elliot said.

He conceded that although there was a very strong and solid movement of private shareholders against the board's proposals, institutional shareholders would support the board. "Because that is the City custom, although there are many who are critical of the board's performance," he added. The group received a tentative takeover offer from Hays last year, valuing Salvesen at 405 pence per share. But Salvesen rebuffed the offer, angering some shareholders. In response, Salvesen has sought to return value by the Aggreko demerger and the dividend payout and moving out of non-core businesses. Rankin confirmed Salvesen is in talks to sell its U.S. refrigerated warehousing business CS Inc. He said the sale would have a major impact on gearing levels and rejected any claims that it was forced. Salvesen announced earlier it was talking to a number of potential buyers and that the divestment was in line with its strategy of focusing resources on core business areas.
